newsitem.title: GERMANY: Perry praises U.S. troop record in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Perry praises U.S. troop record in Bosnia.

text.p: U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry on Monday awarded purple heart medals to two American soldiers wounded by landmines in Bosnia and said U.S. forces had "confounded the sceptics" in the Balkans.

Perry told a ceremony for troops of the U.S. army's First Armoured Division, which led the multinational force into Bosnia last December, that critics had predicted U.S. forces would suffer thousands of casualties and the mission would end in failure.
But he said the force had succeeded in separating warring factions, demobilising armies and their weapons and completing land transfer agreements outlined in the Dayton peace accord.
"You confounded the sceptics," said Perry, who will step down from President Bill Clinton's cabinet in January.
Perry gave the purple heart awards -- given to American soldiers and civilian military workers injured by an enemy or a terrorist -- to army sergeants John Iaccono and Robert Ulrey.

They were among 180 who have suffered injuries since the mission started last December. Six soldiers have died, with one death attributed to landmines and two to vehicle accidents, the U.S. army European command said.

Perry said American troops still in the region as part of the 30,000-strong Stabilisation Force, or SFOR, still faced a difficult situation -- one U.S. military commanders believe may be more difficult than the initial mission.
"The peace in Bosnia is not yet secure. But you have set the standard for your comrades who are equipped and capable to carry on the work you began," Perry said.
